question: What filesystem access policy should OpenClaw support as a maintained security boundary: rule-based `tools.fs` allow/deny paths, `workspaceOnly` only, or a split file-tools plus exec-deny design?
rationale: The current request adds a new config contract and security boundary across tool families, and the open PathGuard PR deliberately leaves arbitrary shell execution outside the boundary.

options.title: Design core tools.fs policy
options.body: Adopt a versioned `tools.fs` allow/deny policy for file/media/apply_patch paths and require the PR/docs to state whether exec is covered or tracked separately.

options.title: Split exec explicitly
options.body: Allow a file-tools-only PathGuard direction only if it links exec coverage to a separate canonical issue and avoids presenting the result as full filesystem sandboxing.

options.title: Keep workspaceOnly only
options.body: Decline path-level config for now and direct operators to Docker, OS-user isolation, and current `workspaceOnly` hardening.

recommendation.title: Design core tools.fs policy
recommendation.body: Adopt a versioned `tools.fs` allow/deny policy for file/media/apply_patch paths and require the PR/docs to state whether exec is covered or tracked separately.
